_about: THE HUMAN CANON, every measure as a fraction of the STATURE (h). This is where a person's proportions are fine-tuned -- the numbers themselves, not the code that builds from them (people.js). A figure is a stature and a build; everything else is here. The numbers are UNISEX: the means of men and women, each taken against their own stature -- segment lengths after Drillis & Contini (1966, the ratios in Winter's Biomechanics), breadths, depths and girths after the ANSUR II survey (2012); a person's sex moves a few widths by the factors under `build.sex`, a child's age its head, hips and legs.

stature._about: how tall each kind comes out: the low end and the span above it, in metres

build._about: widths: a random spread (every width of the body), a child's own factor, then a beast's; then the sex factors on the widths each one moves

sex._about: against the unisex mean, per stature: biacromial .231 / .225, hip breadth .202 / .226, thigh girth .351 / .387, chest depth .145 / .150 (men / women, ANSUR II)

variety._about: HOW PEOPLE DIFFER (people.js bodyOf: drawn from each person's own seeded stream, so the same seed is always the same body). FAT is one number per person, about a bell around 0 (the mean of three draws, `sd` wide), its upper side stretched by `skew` -- most people near the middle, some clearly stout or fat, a few thin -- clamped to [min, max]; a child's and a statue's ideal less (`child`; a physique none), the old's mean higher by `old`. Each unit of it widens what `perFat` names by that share, by sex: a man's goes to the waist and the belly (an apple), a woman's to the hips, the thighs and the bust (a pear); on the thin side (`thinShare`) everything narrows by less. `belly`: the trunk's forward swell over the waist (shell.js TRUNK.pot) per unit. FRAME is the skeleton's breadth, independent of fat: the shoulders and the hips together, `frame` sd; `height` its share of the stature's draw made bell-shaped (the stature's own uniform averaged with one more). Women's and men's face kinds read the same fat as fullness (heads.js `full`: face.json `variety.full`).
variety._fullBins: where the face's fullness steps (heads.js shares one head shape among people of one step): below the first a lean face (-1), from the second stout (1), from the third fat (2)

physiques._about: a figure's IDEAL, over its sex's factors (makePerson `physique`; a statue's: statuary.json `physique`) -- the sculptor's canon, not a survey's: `heroic` (Polykleitos' athlete: the chest broad over a narrow waist, lean hips, full thighs and arms), `classical` (a goddess's: a fuller hip under a narrower waist), `lion` (a Buddha's, after the marks of a great man: shoulders broad and round as a lion's, the waist slim, the arms full). Each width it names is multiplied in; `arms` the upper arm's and the forearm's girth, `neck` the neck's (a carving's had been a stalk under the head). Carved at the survey's mean, a nude's trunk was a box as wide at the hips as at the shoulders

head._about: the CRANIUM's radius, which every other measure of the head and its hair is taken in. A head is .131 of the stature from chin to crown but only .089 across and .113 deep; a cross-section here is a circle, so the sphere is cut between the width and the depth (.1 across), and the jaw below it makes up the height: 1 + jawLength + jawRadius cranium radii.
head._jaw: in cranium radii: how far the head runs on below the skull, and how much it has narrowed by
head._neckRadius: in cranium radii, under the jaw (it widens to the shoulders by neckFoot): a man's (`adult`) about as wide as his jaw, a woman's clearly narrower than hers (`female`: about the mesh face's own neck ring, face.js neckR ~.36 hr -- wider, the column stood out round it from under her jaw up to the ears), a statue's (`ideal`, a physique) as before -- at .64 for both (2026-11-03) a woman's neck stood as wide as her jaw under a mesh face, a man's

torso._about: ONE shape from the crotch to the collar: a round cone flattened front to back, its top a low, squared cap -- the shoulders -- and its bottom a rounder one. The arms hang BESIDE it, clear of it all the way down, so a bodice and a sleeve are two separate sheets that meet at the shoulder.
torso._hip: the hip JOINT (the femur's head), just under the greater trochanter at .53
torso._shoulder: the acromion: h - 1.6 cranium radii - .10 h, which is .815 h for an adult and lower on a child's bigger head
torso._pelvis: the root bone, up the torso from the hip joint, as a fraction of the hip-to-shoulder length
torso._waist: the natural waist (.62 of the stature), as that same fraction: the torso's narrowest ring, where a skirt or a belt sits
torso._armpit: the armpit this far below the acromion: where the shoulders' flare has come in to the chest
torso._rim: the shoulders' edge -- the widest ring of the torso's top -- this far below the acromion
torso._collar: the top of the shoulder cap, where the neck leaves it, this far above the acromion (the cervicale stands at .853, the trapezius's slope reaching the neck at .86)
torso._base: the centre of the torso's bottom ring this far above the hip joint
torso._crotch: the crotch this far below the hip joint (.478 of the stature)
torso._halfWidth: the torso without its arms: at the shoulders' rim (over the shoulder joints, as the deltoid is), the chest under the armpits (.18 across), the natural waist (.165) and the hips (.21, the hip breadth)
torso._depth: the torso's depth as a fraction of its width as DRAWN, the slab under the shell's masses (shell.js TRUNK: the chest's arch, the back, the buttocks), so that the whole comes to the measured chest .145 deep against .176 across, waist .12 against .163, hips .134 against .187; `depthClear` what stands off the trunk (hair, cloth, tools) still measures from
torso._capSquare: how square the shoulders are: the top cap is a superellipse of this exponent (2 is an ellipse, round shoulders; 4 a box)

arm._about: joint to joint: shoulder .795, elbow .64, wrist .494 (atlas: the humerus .823-.644, the radius .647-.514); girths .029 (the deltoid), .027 at the elbow, the forearm .026 to the wrist .0165 (measured skin, .167 and .172 round at the elbow and the forearm's belly, .107 at the wrist). The shoulder joint stands `drop` under the torso's rim and `gap` from its end, so the arm's cap is the end of the shoulder's line, its outer edge .135 from the middle (bideltoid .28 of the stature) -- set clear of the chest instead, it stood out and above the torso as an epaulette with a notch. The arm hangs `abduction` degrees out from the vertical, which takes its shaft off the ribs below the armpit and off the hips.
arm._hand: a real hand is .108 of the stature long (the wrist at .485 h, the fingertips at .377): a flattened pill down the forearm, no fingers at this scale

leg._about: hip joint .52, knee .285, ankle .039 of the stature; the thigh .05 at the top (a girth of .31), the knee .035, the ankle .021; the hip joints .05 either side of the middle, so the thighs meet; the foot .15 long, its heel rFoot round and its toes `toe` of that, the sole flat on the ground (the toes a ball as tall as the heel stood under every hem)
